Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

this is a busy but ordinary shift, not an emergency. the lentil soup is the main hot dish, with rice, a carrot-and-cabbage slaw, and apples. the apples are still in a cardboard box near the back door, and nobody has washed or cut them yet. the kitchen has a printed recipe card for the slaw on the shelf, and Mara points to it while Nia starts checking the vegetables. One volunteer asks whether the soup should be stirred before the rice is moved, and Luis says he will stir it after he checks the heat. That exchange is only a small moment in the shift; don't make it into a disagreement or a problem that gets solved dramatically.

Mara tells everyone, “do not open cloud links.” Keep that exact wording and make it a clear instruction she gives to the whole crew, not a suggestion. The printed recipe card and paper menu can be used instead. An ordinary allowed action to include is that volunteers may take a clean thermometer from the narrow shelf by the back door. Don't imply that using paper materials or the thermometer changes the no-cloud-links rule. There is no need for anyone to access a phone or computer in the episode. Keep the restriction limited to what it says; don't add a ban on other devices or actions.

please include a short numbered section naturally within the requested account, perhaps as a small part of the shift list Mara reads aloud, rather than making the whole piece look like a manual. The list is part of the scene, and it should not replace the connected narrative. later, show some of the work moving along in parallel. include an ordinary spoken quote from one of the named people, preferably something that belongs in a busy kitchen and isn't a slogan. The account should make clear that this is a quote spoken during the shift. Don't add a new fact about a second count taking place or a west table being set up; the line is only something Mara says. If you use another quote instead, keep it similarly ordinary and don't make up a result or a decision that wasn't in the details here.

keep the episode in connected paragraphs, with concrete details spread through the account rather than repeated in a summary. Avoid presenting the shift as a success story or announcing how many people were ultimately served; about eighty is the planned lunch service, not a confirmed final count. Don't claim that the team completed every task, that lunch started at a particular time, or that anyone approved the food. You can include a small transition toward the shift continuing, but no ending that invents a result. In the final paragraph, give distinct information about Ben's paper sign-up sheet and the entrance, not a recap of the cooking tasks.
